EI-kMeans stream detector

Source: R/dfr_eikmeans.R
dfr_eikmeans.Rd

Monitors a stream with an EI-kMeans partitioning (eikmeans()): the first n_train observations form the training sample, and every later window of window_size observations is tested against it. Since it monitors the distribution of the observed features, it is primarily used for virtual concept drift.

Usage

dfr_eikmeans(target_feat = NULL, n_train = 2000, window_size = 200, ...)

Arguments

target_feat

Names of the columns to be monitored. NULL (the default) monitors every numeric column.

n_train

Size of the training sample.

window_size

Size of the tested windows (non-overlapping).

...

Further arguments for eikmeans() (k, alpha, min_points, n_build, thetas).

Value

dfr_eikmeans object. After fit(), drifter_output holds the chi-square statistic and the p-value of every tested window (on its last observation), and obj$model the partitioning.

Details

A drift is reported on the last observation of every window whose p-value is below alpha. reset_state() forgets the partitioning, and the next n_train observations train a new one, which is the adaptation the paper recommends after a drift. Rows with missing values are skipped.

References

Liu, A., Lu, J. and Zhang, G. (2021). Concept drift detection via equal intensity k-means space partitioning. IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics, 51(6), 3198-3211. doi:10.1109/TCYB.2020.2983962

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
# Two clusters; after 3000 rows the right one moves.
set.seed(1)
cluster <- function(n, x) data.frame(x1 = stats::rnorm(n, x), x2 = stats::rnorm(n))
stream <- rbind(cluster(1500, 0), cluster(1500, 5))[sample(3000), ]
drifted <- rbind(cluster(500, 0), cluster(500, 6))[sample(1000), ]
model <- fit(dfr_eikmeans(n_train = 2000, window_size = 200), rbind(stream, drifted))
which(model$drifter_output$p_value < 0.05)
#> [1] 3200 3400 3600 3800 4000
